sound_code_properties: Both modes observe DMA1EN and both DMA1RST/DMA2RST, reflecting shared DMAMUX1 reset. Sticky bools are only in selected mode state, not the ordinary UART state.

Observed retained-domain loss permanently latches domain_lost, retains accepted storage and RX FILLING state, and replaces terminal SUCCESS with STATE without overwriting a prior CANCELLED/TIMEOUT/IO.

Both owned stream and USART3 NVIC disable operations are attempted. DSB/ISB plus independent actual enable-bit reads prove isolation; the algorithm does not confuse IRQ_AVAILABLE or control-call status with enable-off evidence.
If either owned vector cannot be proved disabled, code saves the interrupt mask, observes the platform fault and explicitly loops forever. Other vectors are untouched.
DMA/mux accesses use guarded domain reads/writes. A blocked read returning zero is insufficient for release because withdrawal and final-settle domain predicates must also succeed.

Cache clean and pre/post invalidate execute outside the saved mask while request/FILLING loans remain retained. Reentrant observations remain sticky; callback returns are rechecked before launch/publish.
TX DMA service checks domain after final acknowledgement before active=NULL and SETTLED. RX finish checks after cache, DMA and UART acknowledgements before publish/abort.

RX ordinary-PIO TX service uses the shared private prepare/settle leaves in one saved mask and checks the mode again immediately before its last request access. No new public ABI/registry/second TX machine is added.
Ordinary submit/cancel preserve task-context and argument ordering; pure span/alias checks precede admission. The ordinary transmit IRQ body is byte-identical to the base.

stop_candidate.affected: RX block profile with an accepted shared PIO TX request during port stop.
chain: uart_receive.c stop checks the mode, drains RX and clears DMA duties, then delegates to nx_stm32h743_uart_ops.stop(&s->uart).
Ordinary stop can cancel the shared TX and call ordinary service, whose private prepare/settle path deliberately knows no RX domain.

A real domain loss triggered on the ordinary CR1 source-withdrawal write can therefore occur inside the delegation. Outer mode checks occur only after ordinary stop returns and may be too late if the request was already SETTLED.
stop_candidate.required_real_oracle: No RX stream, real accepted shared PIO TX with progress/TC facts; inject each gateoff/DMA1 reset/DMA2 reset after accepted CR1 withdrawal inside stop. Require original pointer/borrow and Q, BUSY stop, actual owned-vector isolation, and first-terminal preservation.

nonreturn_test_oracle.recommended_change: Explicit ADD_FAILURE after the faulting service call and/or trace.returned=false assertion for the fault branch. Current code already loops forever, so first GREEN coverage is honest and does not justify a manufactured production RED.
nonreturn_test_oracle.author_response: Accepted. Author will separately strengthen the oracle after stop TDD, preserving the earlier source/results and describing bounded observation rather than an infinite-time proof.

external_model_review: DMA1 reset clears the modeled DMA1 engine and DMAMUX1; DMA2 reset clears only DMAMUX1 while preserving DMA1 EN/NDTR/error facts. Gateoff alone does not fabricate DMA completion.
Forbidden DMA/mux accesses are counted, not silently admitted. IRQ enable/pending/active facts are separate and dispatch is refused while the real modeled interrupt mask is saved.

Cache/MMIO callbacks alter external hardware facts rather than private SUT stage fields. Forked Q/fault children retain their storage until parent kill/wait; child termination is not claimed as provider cleanup or actual MCU DMA drain.
